mock_exam.weighting_note: 70% current module (21Q on M6 — all 6 items from levels 21-22 (का/के/की possession) included in full, since those levels fall past the last checkpoint at level 20; 15 more spread across levels 1-20 for breadth) / 30% Phase 2 review (5Q on M4 gender-flagged words, 4Q on M5 sentence grammar) — Module 6 opens Phase 3, so like Modules 1 and 4 before it, the cumulative slice draws on the preceding phase rather than sitting empty.
mock_exam.structural_note: Module 6 has 22 levels, not a multiple of 5, so its 4 checkpoints (after L5/10/15/20) leave levels 21-22 — the का/के/की possession system — uncovered by any checkpoint. All 6 items from those levels are included in the mock.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: की marks a feminine thing owned. बेटा is masculine, and the owner's gender never enters into it.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The marker agrees with बेटी, which is feminine. That राम is masculine is not information the marker uses.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: बेटे is plural, and a masculine plural takes के — the same -े you use on any marked adjective in front of a plural noun.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: का is a postposition like any other, so a Class 1 owner has to go oblique in front of it.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: में makes the possessed noun oblique, and the marker agrees with that noun in whatever state it is in.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: किताब is feminine, so the possessive agrees with it. Whether the owner is a man or a woman never shows up in Hindi at all.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: There is no postposition here, so the plural stays in its direct form बेटे.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: के compounds use the possessive. Leaving हम in its direct form in front of के is not possible.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: में makes the noun phrase oblique, and since स्कूल cannot show it, the adjective must.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: में is a postposition, so कमरा must take its oblique form कमरे.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: Compounds built with के use the possessive form, not the oblique stem. The stem is only for को and से.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: बच्चा replaces its final -ा with the ending. Keeping the -ा and adding on top of it is the single most common plural error in this module.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
options: बड़े लड़कों और बड़ी लड़कियों को
बड़े लड़कों और बड़े लड़कियों को
questions.explanation_en: The first adjective's form does not carry across. लड़कियों is feminine, so the second adjective is बड़ी.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The verb agrees with दूध, which is singular. The plural oblique noun has no effect on it.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: कमरा ends in -ा, so it changes before a postposition — unlike घर, which does not.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: पानी ends in -ी, not -ा, so the Class 1 ending never applies to it.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: लाल has no final -ा to convert into -े. Unmarked adjectives have one form and only one.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: बिल्ला is a separate masculine word for a tomcat. If you mean बिल्ली, it does not change.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The claim is about cities in general, so the plural oblique शहरों is needed.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: Feminine does not mean -ियों. चीज़ ends in a consonant, so it takes -ों like किताब and रात.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: लड़कियाँ is the direct plural and cannot stand before a postposition. के साथ forces the oblique लड़कियों.

questions.prompt_en: Fill the blank: ___ जगह ('place, space, room', my ...).
questions.explanation_en: जगह ('place, space, room') is feminine.

questions.prompt_en: Fill the blank: ___ घर ('house, home', my ...).
questions.explanation_en: घर ('house, home') is masculine.

questions.prompt_en: Fill the blank: ___ चिड़िया ('bird', my ...).
questions.explanation_en: चिड़िया ('bird') is feminine.

questions.prompt_en: Fill the blank: ___ चीज़ ('thing', my ...).
questions.explanation_en: चीज़ ('thing') is feminine.

questions.prompt_en: Fill the blank: ___ सलवार ('salwar, loose trousers', my ...).
questions.explanation_en: सलवार ('salwar, loose trousers') is feminine.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
options: चाय अच्छी है क्योंकि गरम है।
चाय गरम है क्योंकि अच्छी है।
questions.explanation_en: क्योंकि introduces the reason, so the reason has to be the clause that follows it.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The subject is plural, so the verb must be plural too.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: चाय is feminine, so the past form has to be थी.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: आप always takes हैं. हो belongs with तुम, and using it with आप sounds too familiar.
